incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: policy=region-az3-high-packet-loss, severity=page
pagerduty: Triggered on rotation: maria (oncall) -> please acknowledge
maria (oncall): acked, I'm on it. seeing multiple alerts across AZ3 hosts.
ajay (sre): pinging in — what's the symptom? client-side 5xx or infra-level?
maria (oncall): infra checks first: high retransmits, connection resets, some allocator evictions. Frontend 502 spike reported by synthetic checks.
taylor (netops): also seeing BGP flap telemetry around az3-edge-2, route withdraws ~03:12-03:18 UTC. Correlating.
dan (runtime): we just had a rollout in az3 earlier today but rollout completed hours ago. I'll check autoscaler and scheduler logs.
sophie (support): support queue shows several customers reporting intermittent failures for generation endpoints (not all customers). Ticket count increasing.
incident-bot: Related alerts: high-kv-cache-evictions, route-53-healthfail-az3, infra-pod-restarts-az3.
maria (oncall): ok plan: 1) triage impact & scope, 2) if AZ isolated, activate region failover for critical routes, 3) mitigation and rollback if rollout implicated.
ajay (sre): collecting scope: running quick query for failed requests across regions.
ajay (sre): ```sql
SELECT region, count(*) as errors FROM logs.requests WHERE status >= 500 AND ts > now() - interval '15 minutes' GROUP BY region;
```
ajay (sre): results: az3=1789 errors, az1=42, az2=38, eu-west=4. Looks localized to az3.
taylor (netops): confirmed: core switch in az3 shows high CPU and interface errors on fabric100 /eth3. Might be hardware flapping. I've opened a ticket with colo network ops.
maria (oncall): customers affected: internal routing policy shows ~40% of region-az3 traffic failed for last 10min. We'll mark P1 impact for AZ3.
dan (runtime): enabling automated fallback for model-serving routes to prefer az1/az2 for new requests. This will add latency for some clients but reduce errors. Activating now.
dan (runtime): ```sh
redwoodctl route update --selector region=global --fallback region=az1,az2 --priority-az=az1
```
dan (runtime): fallback applied. Traffic shifting. Monitor autoscaler in az1 for burst up.
ajay (sre): autoscaler metrics: az1 CPU up 35%, pod count scaling +20 pods, acceptable headroom.
sophie (support): notifying enterprise customers in affected tenancy buckets; posting status note: "We are investigating increased errors in az3; traffic is being rerouted to healthy regions."
taylor (netops): colo ops confirms noisy neighbor on TOR, they're swapping to standby fabric. ETA 8-12 minutes for physical swap.
maria (oncall): good. keep mitigation: 1) failover stays; 2) reduce new deployments to az3; 3) pause any non-critical rollouts. dan - please block canaries and set rollout freeze.
dan (runtime): done: rollout freeze enforced for az3 and canaries canceled. ```yaml
release_policy:
  az_exclude: [az3]
  freeze: true
```
ajay (sre): digging into pod restarts: kubelet reports OOMKill on a subset of inference workers just before connection errors. Might be related to cache eviction behavior under packet loss.
maria (oncall): ok, add action: if OOM cluster-wide, consider temporary instance type bump or reduce token concurrency per worker. Dan, can you adjust instance sizes if needed?
dan (runtime): I can spin a small hot-pool in az1/az2 to absorb load. Starting instance pool now. ```sh
redwoodctl compute scale --region az1 --pool hotpool --add 8
```
incident-bot: PagerDuty escalation to second on-call (ajay) at 03:22 UTC due to severity threshold.
pagerduty: Acknowledgement received from maria (oncall). Escalation notification sent to taylor (netops).
taylor (netops): fabric swap completed at 03:30 UTC per colo ops, monitors show interface errors dropping to baseline.
ajay (sre): error counts are falling: az3 5xx down from 1789 to 220 in last 10m. Traffic already shifted; per-route success rate improving.
sophie (support): updating status page: "Mitigation in place: Traffic rerouted; engineers working on az3 fabric. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes." Reaction :thumbsup: from several folks.
maria (oncall): question: was today's rollout related? dan said rollout was earlier; but can we get list of services that had a rollout in last 6 hours to be safe.
dan (runtime): listing releases in az3 last 6h: runtime-agent v2.14.1 (no canary), telemetry-collector v1.3.4 (minor), nothing touching networking. I don't think rollout triggered this.
ajay (sre): root cause hypothesis: colo fabric hardware error causing packet loss -> retransmits -> hot path OOMs and scheduler evictions in az3. Secondary contributor: traffic spike to other AZs after fallback causing autoscaler churn but within limits.
maria (oncall): next steps: 1) keep fallback in place until colo confirms stability 2) reconcile OOMs and adjust memory settings 3) run post-incident RCA if fabric had faulty hardware 4) coordinate customer comms.
sophie (support): I'll prepare customer impact timeline and affected customer list, send preliminary advisory to CSMs.
incident-bot: Incident state: active -> mitigation-in-progress. PagerDuty notes: incident_id PD-19382.
maria (oncall): handing off to ajay for next 2 hours for deep-dive. I'll go standby. ajay you are now incident lead.
ajay (sre): taking incident lead. on-call handover ack. I'll coordinate with netops and runtime for RCA.
obs-bot: monitor alert: az3 packet loss normalized at 03:48 UTC; keep watch for 60m.
taylor (netops): colo confirmed switch replaced, firmware patch applied to standby, logs show intermittent PHY resets. They're monitoring.
ajay (sre): marking mitigation: fallback active, rollout freeze, hot-pool scale added. I'll open a tracking ticket PD-19382 and attach logs and timeline.
sophie (support): final note before handoff: customer impact summary drafted, will send to CSMs once ajay confirms.
ajay (sre): thanks. I'll update every 30 minutes and prepare RCA doc after stabilization. closing on-call handoff. :white_check_mark:
